en.title: Heat flow in a rod: model it, measure it, explain the gap
en.background: A thin aluminium rod is heated at one end and cooled in a water bath at the other. The team builds a model of the temperature along the rod, measures it, and explains where and why the two differ.
premises: The rod is 30 cm long and 6 mm across.
Room air is still; the bath is at 21 °C.

steps.name: Set up and measure
steps.q: Build the stand, place four sensors and record a steady temperature profile at three heater powers.

steps.name: Fit the losses
steps.q: Fit the heat-loss coefficient to each profile and say whether one value fits all three.

steps.name: Model and compare
steps.q: Write a finite-difference model, compare it with the data, and explain the largest difference.

en.grading: Each task counts 30 % and the final talk 10 %. Clear plots and honest error bars count more than a perfect fit.
